title: An envelope with an invalid signature is rejected and repeated failures quarantine the connector
description: ConnectorQuarantineService.recordSignatureFailure tracks consecutive failures per connector; the server never trusts an envelope claim (connector_id/tenant_id) without a valid signature verified against the previously-registered public key.
preconditions: A registered connector's real signing public key on file
steps: Send a heartbeat envelope signed with a different (wrong) private key
Repeat past the quarantine threshold
expectedResult: Each invalid-signature envelope is rejected (WS closed with the invalid-signature code); after the threshold, the connector is quarantined and further connections are refused even with a technically valid certificate.

title: The server rejects any envelope whose connector_id/tenant_id disagrees with the mTLS-verified certificate
description: tenant_id and connector_id are resolved ONLY from the certificate the connector authenticated with; a claim inside the envelope payload itself is never trusted as a second source of truth.
preconditions: A valid mTLS connection for connector A
steps: Send an envelope over connector A's connection claiming connector_id/tenant_id belonging to connector B
expectedResult: The connection is closed with the identity-mismatch code; nothing from the envelope is persisted.

title: Masking fails safe for every P1 adapter's real evidence shape, not just a synthetic test record
preconditions: Real fixture data from the LDAP/SQL/REST/SSH-WinRM adapters, each with a deliberately narrow mask_allow_list
steps: Run each adapter's real Collect() output through its configured Mask stage
Inspect the resulting Fields for anything outside the allow-list
expectedResult: No field outside the declared allow-list survives Mask for any of the 4 P1 adapters' real output shapes.

title: LDAP, REST, and SSH/WinRM adapters reject any operation outside their configured allow-list before touching the target
description: Same enforcement-order guarantee as the SQL adapter (VTEC-UNIT-005), verified for the other 3 P1 adapters — no free-form query/command/endpoint ever reaches a real target.
preconditions: Each of LDAP/REST/SSH/WinRM configured with a narrow allow-list
steps: Attempt a Collect() workflow step referencing an operation not on that adapter's allow-list, target pointed at an unreachable endpoint
expectedResult: Each adapter rejects the operation with an allow-list error before any network attempt — confirmed by the absence of any connection-refused/timeout error underneath it.

title: A license key can only ever be redeemed once
preconditions: A freshly-issued license key redeemed once already by connector A
steps: Attempt to register a second connector B using the same license key
expectedResult: The second registration is rejected with invalid_or_expired_license_key; connector B does not obtain a certificate.

title: A non-Enterprise-tier tenant cannot issue a VTEC license key or use any VTEC capability
description: requireFeature('vtec_connector', {strict:true}) gates the entire /api/vtec router — a tenant on Growth/Scale (or with unresolvable entitlements) must be denied outright, never silently degraded to 'allowed'.
preconditions: A test tenant on a non-Enterprise plan
steps: Attempt POST /api/vtec/license-keys and GET /api/vtec/connectors as that tenant
expectedResult: Both requests are rejected with a feature-gate error; no VTEC route is reachable for this tenant regardless of any individual permission grant.

title: Every /api/vtec/* proxy route rejects a caller without the corresponding vtec.* permission
preconditions: A logged-in user with no vtec.* permissions
steps: Call GET /api/vtec/connectors
Call POST /api/vtec/license-keys
Call PUT /api/vtec/connectors/:id/credentials
expectedResult: All three are rejected with a 403/forbidden response; none proxy through to vtec-management-service.

title: A fresh NORMAL_USER has zero vtec.* permissions by default
description: VTEC has no projectId anywhere in its data model, so ProjectMember grants don't apply — access must come from an explicit org-level Extra Permission or a custom Role, never from default NORMAL_USER standing.
preconditions: A freshly created NORMAL_USER with no extra grants
steps: Inspect the user's resolved permission set
Attempt to view the VTEC sidebar entry
expectedResult: No vtec.* permission is present; the VTEC sidebar section and every /vtec/* route are inaccessible.

title: The evidence encryption key and adapter credentials never appear in plaintext in logs or audit trail entries
preconditions: A connector actively resolving a real credential via the relay and encrypting real evidence
steps: Grep the connector's stdout/log output and vtec-management-service's audit log entries for the raw credential value and the raw encryption key
expectedResult: Neither value appears anywhere in plaintext in any log or audit record — audit entries reference the credential by ref name only (e.g. 'credential.read'), never by value.

title: No shell exists in the connector image; docker exec into a running container fails
description: The final image stage is distroless with no package manager, shell, or debug tooling — 'zero local interface' per wiki §02/§09 is meant to hold even against a root-level host compromise.
preconditions: A running hardened connector container built from the real Dockerfile
steps: Attempt docker exec -it <container> sh
Attempt docker exec -it <container> /bin/sh
Attempt docker exec -it <container> /bin/bash
expectedResult: All three attempts fail — there is no shell binary in the image to execute.

title: The container runs non-root with all capabilities dropped and a read-only root filesystem
preconditions: A running hardened connector container via the real docker-compose.yml
steps: docker inspect the running container's User, CapAdd, CapDrop, and ReadonlyRootfs fields
expectedResult: User=10001:10001, CapAdd is empty, CapDrop=[ALL], ReadonlyRootfs=true, and Ports shows no published port.

title: cosign verification rejects a hand-tampered image copy and an image signed with a foreign key
preconditions: A cosign-signed connector image, its public key, and a hand-modified copy of the same image built as a separate digest
steps: Run cosign verify against the original signed digest
Run cosign verify --key <the real public key> against the tampered image's digest
Sign the tampered image with an unrelated key and re-run cosign verify with the original public key
expectedResult: The first verification succeeds; the second fails with 'no signatures found'; the third fails as a signature/key mismatch.
